extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and peer reviewers of systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA 2020), providing a 27-item checklist, an abstract checklist, and flow diagrams to ensure transparent, complete, and accurate reporting of why the review was done, what was done, and what was found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the report as a systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear in the title that the article is a systematic review so readers and indexers can readily identify the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: See the PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts checklist (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PRISMA 2020 abstract checklist to ensure abstracts explicitly state objectives, methods, results (including numbers and effect estimates where applicable), limitations, funding, and registration. The abstract checklist is integrated into PRISMA 2020 and updated to reflect new content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of existing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the review is needed and how it fits with or adds to prior evidence or reviews; situate the review question within the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of the objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the review question(s) clearly (e.g. in PICO or other appropriate format) so readers understand the scope and purpose of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the review and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report eligibility criteria for populations, interventions/exposures, comparators, outcomes, study designs, timeframes, settings, and any other criteria; describe how studies were classified/grouped for each planned synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sources (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify all databases, registers, websites, organisations, reference lists and other sources searched or consulted to identify studies. Specify the date when each source was last searched or consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List every source searched (including database names and registers), organizational or grey literature sources, reference lists, citation searching, and the exact date (day/month/year) of last search for each source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the full search strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including any filters and limits used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete reproducible search strings for each source (databases, registers, websites) including any limits or filters; include search strategies in the main text or supplementary files and reference PRISMA-S where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe screening workflow (title/abstract and full-text screening), roles of reviewers (number, independence), processes for resolving disagreements, and details of any machine-learning or automation tools used (and how they were applied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection process (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the methods used to collect data from reports, including how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, any processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report data extraction forms or templates, independent duplicate extraction procedures, contacting authors for missing information, and any automation tools or data scraping methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items — outcomes (Item 10a)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all outcomes for which data were sought. Specify whether all results that were compatible with each outcome domain in each study were sought (e.g. for all measures, time points, analyses), and if not, the methods used to decide which results to collect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary and secondary outcomes with measurement instruments, time points, and how multiple measures/timepoints were handled or selected; state rules for selecting among multiple results per outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items — other variables (Item 10b)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all other variables for which data were sought (e.g. participant and intervention characteristics, funding sources). Describe any assumptions made about any missing or unclear information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report covariates, subgroup variables, funding/conflict information, study design features, and any imputation or assumptions applied to missing/unclear data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study risk of bias assessment (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies, including details of the tool(s) used, how many reviewers assessed each study and whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which risk-of-bias instruments (e.g., RoB 2, ROBINS-I) were used, procedures for assessment (independent/double review), calibration, and any software or automation used; report how assessments informed synthesis or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect measures (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify for each outcome the effect measure(s) (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference) used in the synthesis or presentation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare the chosen effect measures for continuous and dichotomous outcomes, any transformations performed, and rationale for metric selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — deciding study eligibility per synthesis (Item 13a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis (e.g. tabulating the study intervention characteristics and comparing against the planned groups for each synthesis (item #5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain grouping logic for syntheses, inclusion/exclusion of studies from particular analyses, and how eligibility for each synthesis was determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — data preparation (Item 13b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods required to prepare the data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics, or data conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report approaches for deriving or imputing missing variance/statistics, data conversions (e.g., odds ratio to risk ratio), unit harmonization, and assumptions made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — display methods (Item 13c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to tabulate or visually display results of individual studies and syntheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State presentation formats (forest plots, tables, harvest plots, summary of findings), software used, and decisions about which results to display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — synthesis approach and meta-analysis details (Item 13d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to synthesise results and provide a rationale for the choice(s). If meta-analysis was performed, describe the model(s), method(s) to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity, and software package(s) used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify fixed- vs random-effects models, pooling methods, heterogeneity statistics (I2, tau2), subgroup/meta-regression approaches, and statistical packages (e.g., RevMan, R packages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — exploring heterogeneity (Item 13e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity among study results (e.g. subgroup analysis, meta-regression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned subgroup analyses, meta-regression covariates, sensitivity to study-level characteristics, and the rationale for chosen effect modifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis methods — sensitivity analyses (Item 13f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess robustness of the synthesised results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report analyses testing assumptions (e.g., risk-of-bias exclusions, alternative effect measures, statistical model changes) and how they inform confidence in findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting bias assessment (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe approaches such as funnel plots, statistical tests for small-study effects, trial registry comparisons, and outcome availability assessments to detect publication/reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certainty assessment (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for an outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the framework used (e.g., GRADE), criteria and processes for rating certainty, and how assessments were applied to each outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection — results (Item 16a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the results of the search and selection process, from the number of records identified in the search to the number of studies included in the review, ideally using a flow diagram (see Fig. 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts of records identified, screened, excluded (with reasons), and included; use the PRISMA flow diagram template adapted as needed for original or updated reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection — excluded studies cited with reasons (Item 16b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite studies that might appear to meet the inclusion criteria, but which were excluded, and explain why they were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List notable excluded studies (with citations) and state explicit reasons to enhance transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study characteristics (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite each included study and present its characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide study-level details (participants, interventions/comparators, outcomes measured, settings, sample sizes, key design features) in text or tables to allow assessment of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias in studies — results (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present assessments of risk of bias for each included study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report individual study risk-of-bias judgments (domains and overall), ideally in structured tables or figures, and link these assessments to study results where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of individual studies (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all outcomes, present, for each study: (a) summary statistics for each group (where appropriate) and (b) an effect estimate and its precision (e.g. confidence/credible interval), ideally using structured tables or plots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-study numerical results and effect estimates with intervals, enabling readers to verify pooled analyses and understand study contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of syntheses — summary of contributing studies (Item 20a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each synthesis, briefly summarise the characteristics and risk of bias among contributing studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise which studies contributed to each synthesis, their key features, and collective risk-of-bias concerns that might affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of syntheses — statistical synthesis results (Item 20b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results of all statistical syntheses conducted. If meta-analysis was done, present for each the summary estimate and its precision (e.g. confidence/credible interval) and measures of statistical heterogeneity. If comparing groups, describe the direction of the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report pooled estimates, confidence intervals, heterogeneity metrics (I2, tau2), prediction intervals where appropriate, and clearly state which group is favoured when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of syntheses — investigations of heterogeneity (Item 20c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results of all investigations of possible causes of heterogeneity among study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report subgroup analysis or meta-regression findings, including effect estimates by subgroup, p-values for interaction, and interpretation of heterogeneity sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of syntheses — sensitivity analyses (Item 20d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results of all sensitivity analyses conducted to assess the robustness of the synthesised results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sensitivity analysis outcomes (e.g., excluding high risk-of-bias studies, alternative model specifications) and discuss impacts on main conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting biases — results (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present assessments of risk of bias due to missing results (arising from reporting biases) for each synthesis assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report findings from publication bias analyses, selective outcome reporting assessments, and any influence of suspected reporting biases on syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certainty of evidence — results (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present assessments of certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for each outcome assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide GRADE (or other) certainty ratings per outcome, with brief justifications for downgrades/upgrades and a summary of findings table where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — general interpretation (Item 23a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place findings alongside existing literature, discuss concordance or discordance with prior studies/reviews, and interpret clinical or policy relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — limitations of the evidence (Item 23b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss any limitations of the evidence included in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address study-level limitations (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision) that limit the strength or applicability of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — limitations of the review processes (Item 23c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss any limitations of the review processes used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge limitations such as search constraints, potential selection biases, missing data, language restrictions, or limitations of automation tools and how these may affect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — implications (Item 23d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss implications of the results for practice, policy, and future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable recommendations or suggest research priorities, considering certainty of evidence and applicability to decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and protocol — registration info (Item 24a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide registration information for the review, including register name and registration number, or state that the review was not registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report PROSPERO or other registry identifiers and registration dates, or explicitly state absence of registration to improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and protocol — protocol accessibility (Item 24b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate where the review protocol can be accessed, or state that a protocol was not prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links/locations for protocol documents (journal, registry, repository) or state if none exists; reference PRISMA-P for protocol reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and protocol — amendments (Item 24c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and explain any amendments to information provided at registration or in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document deviations from protocol/registration (with rationale and dates) to allow readers to judge potential bias introduced by changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support (Item 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe sources of financial or non-financial support for the review, and the role of the funders or sponsors in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources, in-kind support, and any involvement of funders in design, conduct, analysis, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests (Item 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any competing interests of review authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full disclosures for financial and non-financial conflicts and explain how conflicts were managed during the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of data, code, and other materials (Item 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report which of the following are publicly available and where they can be found: template data collection forms; data extracted from included studies; data used for all analyses; analytic code; any other materials used in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to repositories (OSF, Dryad, Figshare, institutional repositories), and encourage deposition of supplementary files to support replication, updates, and inclusion in overviews/guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Identify report as systematic review (Abstract Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the report as a systematic review (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label the abstract so readers can immediately identify the article as a systematic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Objectives (Abstract Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of the main objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise the main review question(s) succinctly in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Eligibility criteria (Abstract Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the review (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise statement of key eligibility criteria (population, intervention, outcomes, study types) in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Information sources (Abstract Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the information sources (e.g. databases, registers) used to identify studies and the date when each was last searched (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List main sources searched and the date(s) to inform recency of the search in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Risk of bias methods (Abstract Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly state the risk-of-bias tool or approach used (e.g., RoB 2, ROBINS-I) in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Methods to present and synthesise results (Abstract Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the methods used to present and synthesise results (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether meta-analysis was performed and the general approach to synthesis (statistical pooling, narrative synthesis, SWiM) in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Included studies and participants (Abstract Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the total number of included studies and participants and summarise relevant characteristics of studies (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts of studies and participants and the main features of included studies in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Results for main outcomes (Abstract Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results for main outcomes, preferably indicating the number of included studies and participants for each. If meta-analysis was done, report the summary estimate and confidence/credible interval. If comparing groups, indicate the direction of the effect (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the principal effect estimates with precision and state which group is favoured, mentioning number of studies/participants contributing to the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Limitations of evidence (Abstract Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the limitations of the evidence included in the review (e.g. study risk of bias, inconsistency and imprecision) (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly note key limitations affecting confidence in findings in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Interpretation (Abstract Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a general interpretation of the results and important implications (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise the main interpretation and potential implications for practice, policy, or research in one or two sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Funding (Abstract Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the primary source of funding for the review (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the funding source or declare no funding in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract checklist — Registration (Abstract Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the register name and registration number (abstract level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PROSPERO or other registry identifier in the abstract to facilitate tracking of registered protocols.
